text:
maria: Heads-up — main deploy rolled out and we're seeing a p99 spike on small-chat workloads. Before the merge p99 ~42ms, after merge it's ~120ms on the same single-tenant test harness. Tried a couple restarts, same result.
aj: ugh, rough. which merge? commit? :eyes:
maria: merge PR #6422 — changed kernel selection heuristics + a batching tweak. stack: runtime v2.8.1 -> v2.9.0 merge sha f4a7e2d
sam: can you paste the perf numbers and the run command you used?
maria: run: `./tools/perf_runner --model small-chat --concurrency 8 --iterations 500 --profile` output snippet:
```
p50 8.9ms
p90 23.2ms
p95 36.7ms
p99 119.8ms
median tokens/sec 820
```
Before merge p99 ~42ms on the same machine.
kevin: did we change kv-cache logic in that PR? last time kv invalidation blew up latency on short requests.
maria: PR touched kernel selector and batching policy. There was also a microchange in kv_cache: strip_prefix during lookup to normalize keys (very small). not sure that would cause this.
claira: perf-bot just flagged CI: `p99-latency-gate (main)` failed after that merge.
perf-bot: CI alert: p99-latency-gate failed on main for runtime integration tests (delta +185%). See job: https://ci.redwood/12345
aj: let's run a git-bisect locally ASAP. volunteer to run if you share a minimal repro.
maria: starting git bisect now. initial bad=main (f4a7e2d)
```
git bisect start f4a7e2d v2.8.1
git bisect run ./tools/perf_bisect_helper.sh --filter p99
```
(Using the standard perf_bisect_helper which runs 200 iters and checks p99)
aj: while that's running, try reproducing with `--disable-kernel-fallback` and `--kv-cache-prefetch=off` flags — if one of those flips the perf back we can narrow the area quickly.
sam: bisect output so far (interrupted print):
```
bisect log: tested commits up to abcde12, 4/23 good, 6/23 bad -> narrowing
profile: heavy time in aten::memmove and in kernel_selector::choose_fast_kernel
flamegraph: big hotpath in batcher::pack_batches
```
maria: interesting — pack_batches shows increased memcpy at token concat stage. that smells like a packing layout change in the batching patch.
kevin: that could be quantized kernel path selecting a different kernel that requires additional rearrange. maybe we added a fallback path triggering extra copies.
claira: any chance the runtime now prefers aten kernels over our fused kernel for short sequences? that would explain memmove and latency.
aj: bisect found first bad at commit 3b7c91a — diff shows heuristic change: prefer_kernel="best_estimate" -> "cost_model_v2" and change to pack threshold i.e. pack_max_tokens decreased from 2048 -> 512.
maria: lowering pack_max_tokens would cause more smaller batches which usually hurts throughput but shouldn't spike p99 that much unless it triggers a slow kernel.
sam: I built that commit locally and ran the perf. With `--disable-kernel-fallback` p99 drops back to ~48ms. With fallback enabled p99 ~115ms. So kernel fallback seems to be picking a slower kernel for short batches.
kevin: confirm which kernels: attach small mapping I printed from runtime
```
selected kernel: aten_gemm_int8 (slow path)
fallback triggered: yes
fallback reason: quant_conv unsupported for sequence_len<=32
```
claira: so the heuristic change + reduced pack_max_tokens increased fallbacks on short sequences -> triggers aten path -> memcpy blowup. Good find.
aj: can we hotfix by increasing pack_max_tokens back to 2048 in a config OR change fallback condition to prefer quant_conv when available? Which is less risky?
maria: fast patch option: revert pack_max_tokens change in dedicated rollout branch to unblock customers. longer fix: update kernel selector to prefer quantized fused kernel for short sequences when supported, and add a micro-optimized memcpy path.
sam: I'll open a PR today: revert config change + add a test that asserts selected kernel for small-chat workload is `quant_conv_fused` on CI.
perf-bot: CI job queued: `p99-latency-gate (try-revert-6422)`
aj: also add a smoke perf test that runs with `--kernel-fallback` toggled; we should catch this next time.
kevin: one more thought — does kv_cache strip_prefix change affect key lookup cost? maybe increases lookup misses and causes extra cache population work.
maria: checked kv cache metrics — miss rate unchanged. this is purely kernel-selection induced.
claira: plan summary: (1) open revert PR to restore pack_max_tokens -> immediate rollout block removal, (2) add regression test for kernel selection on short sequences, (3) later change kernel selector to prefer quant_conv when safe and add optimized memcpy path, (4) follow-up: perf postmortem and checklist for kernel heuristics changes.
aj: agreed. maria can you paste the bisect commit id and PR link so eng-sre can watch deploys?
maria: bisect culprit: 3b7c91a (PR #6422), revert PR drafted: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/6481
sam: running CI on revert now, will post results in 10–15m.
perf-bot: CI result: `p99-latency-gate (try-revert-6481)` succeeded — p99 restored to baseline.
claira: excellent. leaving this thread pinned for follow-up work items. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
maria: moving postmortem draft to #postmortems and will link to this thread. Closing rollout blocker.
